summary: Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar educated at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (doctorate ~1969–1973), and Munich (Habilitation ~1986–1990). He was a professor at the University of Chicago (1990–2011) and later taught at the Geneva Graduate Institute (2013).

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Barend Jan Terwiel by 2004. He held an affiliation at Hamburg (attested 2004) and served on the Pali Text Society Council (attested 2026).

Martin Straube is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2026, he was attested at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes (attested 2002). He also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a McGill instructor.

Martin Willson was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2012) and had Lambert Schmithausen as her MA supervisor. She has worked as a researcher at the University of Vienna.
Martine Kropman is an Indology scholar who conducted doctoral research at the University of Groningen and Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter Bisschop (attested 2026).
Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also been mentored by Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He held an academic post at the University of Michigan from ~1949 to 1990.
Mary Anne Cartelli is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Philip B. Yampolsky (attested 1999).

Mary Clabaugh Wright was a Sinologist and historian educated at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (PhD ~1951). She served as curator of Stanford's China collection (1947) and later became an associate professor (1959) and full professor (1964) at Yale.

Mary Evelyn Tucker works in religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at SUNY, Sophia, Fordham, and Columbia (PhD ~1985), she held posts at Bucknell (Professor ~1989–2006), Harvard (~1995–2006), and Yale (Professor ~2006).

Mary Haas was a linguist who studied under Edward Sapir, with degrees from Earlham, Chicago, and Yale (~1931–1935). She held a long-term academic appointment at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1943 to 1977.
Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007).

Mary Margaret McCabe is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She was a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990) and Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), later joining University College London.

Mary Shepherd Slusser worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at Michigan, Columbia (PhD ~1950), NYU, and Harvard. She worked for the U.S. State Department (1951–1958) and held posts at the National Museums of African and Asian Art.

Marybeth White is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed a double major honors degree at York University and became a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Maryla Falk was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1934–1938) and was a member of the Polish Oriental Society and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology who was mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She held a professorship at Smith College (attested 1986).

Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history who completed his degrees, including a doctorate (1980), at Kyoto University. He served as a Kyoto University professor (1981–1993) before becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).
